Kazzaken  You're so wrong. They skipped old APIs and lower res high FPS at the hardware level and that can't be fixed by software, only mitigated. They are emulating DX9 on the driver side, concurrents kept the translation layer in silicon.
If the perf discrepancy was shown on specific game engines independently from the resolution., we could point out a lack of driver optimization but it's not the case here.

author: @PainterVierax

text:
Kazzaken  Vulkan and DX12 are low level. For older APIs the stack needs additional translation layers, Intel decided to implement them inside the driver instead of dedicating some transistors, that's all.
Sure you can optimize that software but that's the same reason why Nvidia driver overhead pops up time to time and makes Radeon products more performant in some scenarios.
Moreover your Proton analogy is flawed. DXVK will always have some overhead. When the performance is better, it's just because Windows is removed from the equation.
A good analogy is like CISC vs RISC: both internally can use the same micro-arch with the same micro-ops but the CISC arch has extra translation layers in silicon to avoid entirely relying on compliation optimizations. The third case is like when Qualcomm or Apple can't legally implement x86 translation layers in silicon and have to rely entirely on software. The latter is the worst case and this is merely what Intel did here.
